transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Thank you. Well, I'm here because... I've started catching myself having these thoughts. I keep thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And sometimes, usually on the drive home from school, I start wondering if my family and my students would just be better off without me around. It really scares me, honestly, because I don't want to actually act on it or do anything to hurt myself. But the thoughts are there, and I knew I needed to come in.
I'm really glad you came in to talk about this. Aside from these thoughts, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless?
I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed feeling sad, exactly... like, I'm not crying all the time or anything. I just mostly have those thoughts I mentioned.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have noticed that. I used to really look forward to things like playing softball, going to my book club, or just working in my garden. And even the robotics club I help run at school. But lately, I mostly just go through the motions if I do go... or I just end up canceling my plans altogether. None of it really feels enjoyable anymore.
About how long have you been feeling this loss of interest and having these thoughts?

It's been... well, a while now. I'd say it's been going on for about a year and seven months. It started right around the time I took over the STEM assessment redesign at school, which was just added on top of my regular teaching load.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns during this time?

Yeah, my sleep has definitely been affected. I can be completely exhausted, but I'll still just lie awake in bed, replaying assessment deadlines and classroom mistakes in my head. And then... when I do finally fall asleep, I usually wake up around 4 a.m., and I never really get back to sleep after that.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

No, I don't think so. This is the first time it's been like this. I mean, I've been stressed before, especially during finals or when the school year starts, but... it's never been this bad, or lasted this long. I've never felt this empty before.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, wired, or needed much less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

No, I haven't. Um... I've never really felt wired like that. Even before all this started, I always needed a normal amount of sleep just to get through the teaching day. So, no, I haven't ever had a time where I didn't need to sleep or felt unusually energetic.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight during this time?

Yeah, I have. Most school days, I just forget to eat, or I end up avoiding it until late in the afternoon. And my weight has definitely dropped... over the past year, my clothes have gotten noticeably looser, even though I'm not trying to lose weight at all.
Have you been experiencing persistent fatigue or a lack of energy nearly every day?

Yes, definitely. I just... I have no energy at all. By the time I get through teaching my classes and sitting through a department meeting, my body just feels so heavy. Even doing small things, like making dinner or trying to answer a few parent emails... it just feels like climbing a steep hill. I'm just exhausted all the time.
